collision_energy.official_meaning: A list of electron-volt collision energies. One value denotes one acquisition; several values denote a spectrum merged from acquisitions at different energies. collision_energy_orig also describes multi-value entries as merged single-energy acquisitions.
collision_energy.applies_to_20_50: By the published column convention,[20,50] describes multiple recorded acquisition energies that were merged, not evidence of a continuous20–50eV interval or ramp.
collision_energy.unknown: No merge weighting, raw-count weighting, per-acquisition normalization sequence, or detailed instrument acquisition schedule is specified by this page.
collision_energy.modeling_implication: Comparing forward predictions at each recorded CE and fusing them against the current midpoint35eV approximation is a justified experiment. Equal-weight/max/intensity-normalized fusion is a modelling choice and must not be described as reproducing the instrument's actual merge.
collision_energy.conversion_caveat: For training sources, collision_energy_ev is best-effort; NCE-to-eV is approximate and can be null when unresolved. Do not treat all source CE metadata as equally accurate.

public_frontier.common_difference_from_our_v8: Their larger stack combines independent spectral/analog/ranker channels, popularity signals, external structure proposals and two forward scorers. Our verified v8 is original FPNet single over existing712K pool plus GLACIER fusion. This architectural gap is evidence of omitted channels, not evidence that each omitted channel improves our pipeline.

research_implications: v8 provides real hidden-scoring evidence for the combined pipeline change(+0.101); no newer score exists in the returned submission history.

005's ICEBERG-vs-GLACIER full-NP result supports a controlled forward-scorer comparison using the same candidate windows and fusion normalization. It does not already guarantee another hidden improvement.
Collision-energy lists represent merged acquisitions. Compare multi-CE predicted-spectrum fusion against midpoint approximation while keeping candidate pool, adduct and downstream ranking fixed.

Do not let popularity priors, additional PubChem proposals, changed fingerprints, new rankers and new forward models enter one experiment together; source-confidence calibration can be studied on labelled candidates separately.

Keep the005 conclusions: LMSD did not improve labelled recall, ranker lost badly when the true structure lacked reference spectra, and FRIGID was not actually spectrum-conditioned. Latest public-source anecdotes do not overturn those findings.
No fixed class proportions can be inferred from0.307, current top scores, the ID-leak thread or unsubstantiated notebook prose.
